items.title: 56422_Leonard Phillips oral history interview
items.q: Jack Teagarden played a hell of a solo on it. ... So he's the one that changed the trombones around. Everybody then was copying him.

ctx.x: That's a recording by Red Nichols?

Yeah. Jack Teagarden played a hell of a solo on it. He had everybody... See, because Jack Teagarden changed trombone around. See, before he came along, cats was playing slide horn. So they said, "DA-AA-AAT..." But he come along, "BUH-DA-BE/DAH-DA-BE/DA-DAT, BAH-BAH-BAH-BO, BAH-BU-BAH-BO-DA-BU..." -- playing on of them things, playin' riffs. Only it wasn't slide. So he's the one that changed the trombones around. Everybody then was copying him. Like, all trombone players.
Did you ever hear Jimmy Harrison back then?
